rules.coverage_note: A named form action -- a member of the `actions` object in `+page.server`. The members are `definition.method`: omega-javascript declares an object-literal member that way whatever its value is, and a nested arrow function inside an action body is the `definition.function` that this rule used to pick up instead.
Which route accepts form posts: the exported `actions` object of a +page.server module is what answers a POST to that route.
Which routes have a server endpoint, including a +server module whose methods are re-exported (`export { GET } from './impl'`) and therefore never declared here.
Which handler answers POST on this route: a function named for an HTTP method declared in a +server file, and the route its directory spells.
The same endpoint handler when it is bound to a name rather than declared -- `export const GET = async (event) => ...`, which TypeScript states as definition.variable.
Where this route's error boundary is. +error.svelte declares nothing at all, so no Pack fact but the artifact names it.
What runs on every request before any route does: the hooks a project installs, and which of hooks.server / hooks.client / hooks each one belongs to.
The same hook when it is a named binding -- `export const handle = sequence(a, b)` is the common spelling.
That this project installs hooks, when the hook is re-exported or composed rather than declared (`export { handle } from './mw'`).
Which files reach for SvelteKit's own virtual modules: $env/static/private, $env/dynamic/private, $app/state, $app/navigation, $lib. This is what answers 'which code reads a server-only secret'.

Which layouts wrap this page. A +layout.svelte applies to every route in its own directory and below, so the join is the layout's directory being an ancestor of the page's path; every ancestor layout is stated.
Which directory a layout wraps, from the file alone. A +layout.svelte that is plain markup around <slot/> emits no component tag.
The layout of a route directory and the components it renders around every page below it. Keyed by file, because a layout is not a URL.
What data this route loads before it renders. The module the `load` is declared in says where it runs: +page.server/+layout.server are server-only, +page/+layout are universal.
The same loader when `load` is a named binding rather than a function declaration.

Which route serves this path, from the file alone. A +page.svelte that is static markup declares nothing and emits no component tag, so the declaration-entered rules never see it; the artifact fact does.
What this route renders: the page component of the directory, and each Svelte component it puts on the page. A component tag is the one markup fact the Svelte Pack states by name.
Where the matcher a route segment names is defined: `[id=integer]` resolves to the `match` exported by src/params/integer, so the matcher is keyed by the name the route spells, not by its path.
The same matcher when `match` is a named binding rather than a function declaration.
The matcher name a route spells as [id=integer] is the file stem, not a declaration; this states it from the file so a matcher whose `match` is re-exported still exists.
The same for +layout.ts / +layout.server.ts: the layout module belongs to this route directory whether or not it declares a load.
Which files make up this route, and that the route exists, for a +page.ts or +page.server.ts that exports no load, actions or route option.
Which routes set a page option -- prerender, ssr, csr, trailingSlash, config, entries. The option's value is not stated: the Pack names the declaration, not what it is assigned.

gaps: a +page.svelte that renders no component is not stated as a Page: the Svelte Pack names component tags, not files
an individual form action is stated only where the Pack emits a function held by an object property, which omega-javascript does and omega-typescript does not
a page option's value (prerender = true vs false) is not stated: the Pack names the declaration, not what it is assigned
which route segment uses which param matcher needs the `[id=integer]` segment parsed, which no Pack states
adapter behaviour, matcher execution and runtime handle/action invocation remain runtime semantics

reconciliation.v3_144: Pack/Framework fact contract reconciled against current host Pack; runtime-only/dynamic gaps remain explicitly bounded.
